solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rogue talks about freestyle boxing ring

parts.note: raps are talks, as in a rap session or a chat
C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the freestyle word encloses the ring like a boxer's guard, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: all-in wrestling is the freestyle kind with few rules
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A villain who chats while fighting without rules inside a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' is the containment signal here, not the sport; all-in wrestling is the no-holds-barred kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or scamp is a rogue; both name a likeable villain.

clue.text: Bird runs with Bertie when topless?

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the surname is cut off

parts.note: Bertie Wooster is P. G. Wodehouse's comic toff

explanation.surface: A question about a bird, a sprint and a famous fictional gent losing his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is the hapless young gentleman of P. G. Wodehouse's Jeeves stories; 'when topless' removes his W.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel, the male domestic fowl, is a farmyard bird.

clue.text: Annoy Prince Bertie's man unlimitedly?

indicators.note: without its limits, the valet's name loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: Jeeves is the valet of Bertie Wooster in Wodehouse

explanation.surface: A royal endlessly irritating a famous fictional valet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimitedly' strips both ends of the name of Wodehouse's unflappable valet.
explanation.definitionFit: To irk or vex someone is to annoy them; a pet hate is the noun sense.

clue.text: Most huggable idle stud condemned by Conservative

indicators.note: damned or wrecked words get their letters thrown into new order

explanation.surface: A Tory denounces a lazy womaniser, who is nonetheless very cuddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' rearranges IDLE STUD into UDDLIEST, which follows C.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of cuddly describes whoever is easiest to embrace.

clue.text: Welshman's second and second to last in record jump

indicators.note: the two chosen letters sit inside the record abbreviation

parts.note: LP, long-player, is a vinyl record
the second letter of the word Welshman is E
the second to last letter of the same word Welshman is A

explanation.surface: A Welsh athlete records a jump on his second and penultimate attempts.
explanation.walkthrough: WELSHMAN's second letter is E and its second to last is A; 'in' puts EA inside LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound or spring is a jump; the verb and noun both fit.

clue.text: Prisoner keeps note close

indicators.note: the convict holds the note within, as a keeper holds something

parts.note: an inmate is a prisoner
TI (te) is the seventh note of sol-fa

explanation.surface: A prisoner holds on to a letter that is near at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is the adjective, as in a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate friend is a close one, sharing private confidences.

clue.text: Dancing reel this time could be lengthier

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new arrangement
the mixed letters of the answer and the reel together could be the final word

parts.note: taken as written: its letters are the pool

explanation.surface: A reel danced at this hour might go on for longer.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus REEL, mixed, make LENGTHIER; strip R, E, E, L from it and NGTHI remain to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time when reels are danced, so 'this time' points to the hours after dark.

clue.text: Grid has dodgy wiper

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A grid with a faulty windscreen wiper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges GRID HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for washing plates is used to wipe them, so it is a wiper.

clue.text: Rant promoted assistance to be leading race

indicators.note: the assistance piece comes ahead of the race piece
in a down clue, promoted words move up, so the help word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is assistance
a tribe is a people or race

explanation.surface: Someone moved up the ranks to help a leading race, then sounds off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns AID upwards into DIA, which leads TRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter tirade or harangue is a rant.

clue.text: Left unwise to adopt Right's facility

parts.note: left over means remaining

indicators.note: the silly word takes in the right letter as one adopts a child

parts.note: daft means silly or unwise
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political tale of the Left foolishly embracing the Right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political but means remaining; 'to adopt' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank's arrangement letting a customer borrow beyond the balance is a borrowing facility.

clue.text: Group of prison rejects in Porridge?

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for group

indicators.note: throwing back the slang word for jail sends its letters the other way

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Inmates turning their noses up at prison porridge, or the sitcom Porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is also a BBC sitcom set in a prison, which feeds the misdirection. 'rejects' turns STIR into RITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse ground maize boiled into a breakfast mush is a type of porridge in the American South.

clue.text: Heartlessly shake very big drink

indicators.note: losing its heart, the shaking word gives up its central letter

parts.note: tremble means shake

explanation.surface: A cruel order to shake up an enormous cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple measure of spirits is a very large drink in a pub.

clue.text: Copier, one with German schedule from the east

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mit is German for with

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A photocopier that works with a German timetable from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic or someone who apes others is a copier.

clue.text: Saint framed by libertine died excited

indicators.note: the saint is surrounded by the rake like a picture in a frame

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man

explanation.surface: A holy man set up by a rake dies in a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred up or aroused, as passions are, means excited.

clue.text: In Beirut, possibly an inhabitant there?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A question whether someone in Beirut is a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BEIRUT and AN; 'there' points back to Beirut, a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A city dweller is an inhabitant of a city such as Beirut.

clue.text: Support adopting suitable backing, or close

indicators.note: the support takes the other piece in, as a family adopts a child

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm

indicators.note: backing means read in reverse

parts.note: fit means suitable

explanation.surface: A supporter chooses suitable backing, or comes near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses and 'adopting' inserts. 'close' is the weather sense, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is hot and airless, the same as suffocating.

clue.text: Make criticism of playing unfit and lame

indicators.note: the words are put in play and arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A pundit criticising a player who is both unfit and lame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges UNFIT and LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail or protest loudly is to make criticism.

clue.text: Celebrity benefit for such as Capaldi when compared to Davison?

definitions.text: such as Capaldi when compared to Davison?

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity
for the sake of means for the benefit of

explanation.surface: A star benefit compares two famous actors, Capaldi and Davison.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Capaldi and Peter Davison both played Doctor Who; sharing the first name Peter, each is the other's namesake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing a name with another person is that person's namesake, as two Peters do.

clue.text: Denial about bottom is sincere

indicators.note: the sincere word goes about the bottom, wrapping around it

parts.note: real means genuine or sincere
butt is slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone insists, without joking, that they did not touch a bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the sincere word wraps around the other; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A refutation or contradiction of a claim is a denial.

clue.text: Resistance fighter expels British snake

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: the fighter throws out the British letter

parts.note: a battler is a fighter

explanation.surface: A wartime resistance fighter throws out a British snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance fighter' reads as one wartime phrase, but it splits into two pieces; 'expels' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rattlesnake is commonly called by this shortened name.

clue.text: Easy infection by hospital department

parts.note: flu is a viral infection
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: An easy infection caught in a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth, effortless speech is easy and flowing.

clue.text: Head off scare following flier's doomed craft

indicators.note: the scare piece follows the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a flier

indicators.note: the head of the fright word is taken off, removing its first letter

parts.note: a panic is a scare

explanation.surface: Avert a scare after a pilot's ill-fated aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as avert but means drop the first letter; 'following' puts the bird first.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Star liner that sank in 1912 is the most famous doomed ship.

clue.text: Ineffectual player, fool to turn over King and two Queens

indicators.note: turning over the fool word reverses its letters

parts.note: nit is a fool
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER (Elizabeth Regina) twice

explanation.surface: A useless card player, foolish enough to turn over a king and two queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' makes NIT into TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fiddles and dabbles without real skill is an ineffectual player.

clue.text: Result such as 4-3 at the start?

parts.note: four is an even number
the number three, written out, starts with T

explanation.surface: A football score of 4-3, decided early.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome, as in the event of something happening, is a result.

clue.text: Drive around start of tailback?

indicators.note: the drive word is turned around into a new order
only the opening letter of the queue word is used

explanation.surface: An instruction to drive round the beginning of a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges DRIVE, and 'start of' gives T from tailback.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute traffic around a jam is to send it on a detour.

clue.text: Put out command to include 5, not 500

indicators.note: the order word is to take in a new numeral
the old numeral is dropped in its favour

parts.note: an edict is a command
D is the Roman numeral for 500
V is the Roman numeral for 5

explanation.surface: An order to include five rather than five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap D for V in EDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a tenant out of their home is to put them out.

clue.text: Head upset amateur swimmer

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A swimmer, an amateur, upset by a head injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NUT into TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ocean fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: Allow that man to find oblivion

parts.note: to let is to allow
he refers to that man

explanation.surface: Letting a man find blissful forgetfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth, drinking from the underworld river of this name brings forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical river of forgetting stands for oblivion itself.

clue.text: Praise grown-up concealing a negative bit of information in review

indicators.note: the grown-up hides the article within

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up

indicators.note: reviewing goes back over, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: no is a negative

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word information

explanation.surface: A grown-up reviewer hides a damning snippet among the compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' signals an insertion of the article; 'in review' reads the negative plus I backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive admiration or flattery is praise.

clue.text: Tea brewed with their cup is beneficial

indicators.note: brewing stirs the tea and the cup words into a fresh blend

explanation.surface: A cup of brewed tea is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges TEA and THEIR CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Healing or restorative treatment is beneficial to health.
